Normalize activations with batch statistics and running estimates.

Before Flatten or a global pool (after Conv2D, in [H, W, C] images) it is BatchNorm2D: one mean and variance per channel over the batch and every pixel (torch BatchNorm2d). After Flatten it is BatchNorm1D: one per feature of [batch, features]. Training updates the running mean and variance; evaluation and testing reuse those estimates.

## Settings

| Group | Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normalization | Epsilon | `eps` | Number | `1e-5` | `0.000000001-3.402823e38` | The run | Positive numerical stability term. Required. |
| Normalization | Momentum | `momentum` | Number | `0.1` | `0.0-1.0` | The run | Running-statistics update momentum. Required. |
| Fine-tuning | Frozen | `frozen` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | Keeps this layer's weights as they are while the rest of the model trains: no gradient step, no weight decay, no optimizer memory. Use it on layers that start from a weights file (fine-tuning), then turn it off to train them too. |
| Fine-tuning | When frozen | `frozen_statistics` | Choice | `keep` | `keep` (Keep its statistics), `update` (Keep updating statistics) | The run | What a frozen BatchNorm does with its running mean and variance. Keep its statistics: it normalises with the loaded values, as in evaluation (usual for fine-tuning on small data). Keep updating statistics: the weights stay but the statistics follow the new data, as PyTorch does when only requires_grad is off. |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Usage

```text
Place after convolution/dense, before or after activation (debated).
```

## Tips

- Essential for deep networks - enables training very deep models.
- Has different behavior in training vs inference mode.
